**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate all requested exhibition state before completing**

When `configure_image_exhibition` waits for `loadAllTextures()`, the normal view, playback, physics, and gravity controls remain active. If a user changes any of those settings during that wait, this check verifies only the selected artist, so the tool reports `complete` even though the resulting state no longer matches the requested configuration. Capture and compare all requested fields before returning, or prevent concurrent UI changes.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Rerun LSP checks instead of rebinding stale responses**

This changes the receipt to the new source revision while retaining the earlier `executionIdentifier`, timestamp, and MCP responses; the added `bindingHistory` merely asserts that selected inputs stayed unchanged. `run-formal-check.mjs` only compares this top-level `sourceRevision` with the current manifest and evaluates the stored responses—it never validates `verifiedInputs` or the rebinding history—so this causes the current proof report to pass without running the six LSP checks for this revision, contrary to the stale-evidence behavior documented in `README.md:48`. Preserve the original revision and rerun the MCP checks, or implement and validate scoped evidence reuse before marking the new revision as covered.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Regenerate the browser evidence against the final sources**

This receipt does not describe the committed implementation: the recorded `main.mjs` digest is `74511e…`, while this commit contains `7c7e7f…`; the recorded geometry and world digests likewise differ from their committed files. These files contain the final collision-loading, color-output, and scene changes, so the claimed on-screen navigation and collision results were obtained from an earlier revision and cannot validate the code being reviewed. Regenerate the browser run after the final changes or clearly mark this receipt as superseded.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind the receipt to the committed source digest**

For the recorded `sourceCommit`, a clean archive evaluated by `scripts/source-revision.mjs` produces `sha256:195980a457dfe88b376ca59c55f018a7f38dd97e81881c6cec38931ddf5a98b1`, not the stored `81baf2…` value. The latter manifest includes 33 generated files under the gitignored `web/public/cosmos/` directory, which are absent from both the commit and its archive. Consequently the publication receipt and the pass reports keyed to this revision cannot be authenticated from the committed source; generate the revision before staging these outputs or exclude that generated directory.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Avoid loading full originals for every thumbnail**

On a wide desktop, all 15 buttons fit in or near the visible horizontal strip, so assigning every thumbnail the original `image_url` causes the browser to fetch the entire 35.9 MiB image set during the initial single-image view; `loading="lazy"` does not defer images already near the viewport. This defeats the intended on-demand loading and substantially slows first load, especially on constrained connections. Use dedicated thumbnail assets or assign each thumbnail source only when it enters the strip viewport.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Align the collector with HEAD reconciliation**

When a `Link` navigation produces the HEAD/`ERR_ABORTED` sequence this change is intended to accept, the committed collector cannot satisfy these predicates: `mcp/chrome-measurements.js:25-29` never creates `run.requests` and records the failure text as `reason` without a request method, while this code requires `requests`, `failure.method`, and `failure.error`. Moreover, that collector sets `run.functional` to false whenever `failedRequests` is nonempty at lines 153-155. Consequently an actual capture still classifies the route transfer as unknown and the Chrome functionality gate as failed; update the capture schema and compute functionality after reconciliation rather than only adjusting the synthetic fixture.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Populate the request trace required by classification**

When measurements are produced by the checked-in `mcp/chrome-measurements.js`, the run object never receives a `requests` property: the collector only retains `errors`, `failedRequests`, and `interactions` at line 42. Consequently `isConfirmedHeaderCheck` always rejects the extensionless `HEAD /records/` timing, so the transfer remains unclassified and `summary.complete` stays false in the exact scenario this change is intended to fix. Record the request URL, method, and resource type in the collector before requiring that evidence here.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Emit the failure fields used for reconciliation**

The checked-in collector records a failed request as `{ url, reason }` at `mcp/chrome-measurements.js:28`, whereas this predicate requires `failure.method` and `failure.error`. Thus an actual `net::ERR_ABORTED` notification can never enter `reconciledRequestFailures`, even after the successful HEAD response is classified. Update the producer and consumer to use the same failure-record schema.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Base functionality on the reconciled failure set**

In the intended HEAD-abort scenario, `mcp/chrome-measurements.js:153-156` has already set `run.functional` to false because it requires `failedRequests.length === 0`. Requiring `run.functional === true` here therefore prevents a real reconciled abort from ever producing a functional stage; the test misses this because it appends the failure after constructing a fixture whose `functional` flag is already true. Recompute the relevant functional conditions after reconciliation or change the collector's flag semantics.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

## 完了条件

- [ ] 現在の対象で言語サーバーの6種類の検査を実行し、各対象定理の公理依存を確認する。
- [ ] 過去の実行時刻・応答・版番号を保全する。

issues.body:
## 起きていること

作家ボタンの縮小画像にも原画像のURLを設定しています。横幅の広い画面では多数のボタンが読み込み範囲に入り、一枚ずつの表示でも原画像一式の通信が発生します。レビューにある35.9メビバイトは当時の指摘値として扱い、現在の容量は別途測定します。

## 完了条件

- [ ] 縮小表示用の軽い画像を使うか、必要なボタンだけ画像を取得する。
- [ ] 幅の広い画面と狭い画面で、最初に読み込む原画像数と通信量を測定する。
- [ ] 作家を切り替えたときに必要な原画像が表示される。
- [ ] 原画像と出典を保全する。
